title: Chapter 113: A Brave Idea
html:
“You heard them mention that?” Chen Ge’s interest was piqued.

“Yes. The day before they disappeared, your parents came to see me. Someone wanted to give me a present but could not come in person, so they delivered it on that person’s behalf.” Director Luo took a wooden box from a shelf. Inside was a roughly carved roly-poly toy.

He balanced it in his palm. “The workmanship is crude, but I appreciate its meaning. No matter how often it falls, it always stands again.”

Anxiety sharpened Chen Ge’s voice. “What did my parents say afterward? Where did you hear them?”

“They left after giving me the present. I tend to keep my office door open, so I overheard them in the corridor.” Director Luo searched his memory. “They hadn’t gone far. Your father said something like, ‘The door to the Third Sick Hall has opened again.’ Your mother replied, ‘It was never closed in the first place.’”

“That’s it?”

“That’s all I could hear. They did continue the conversation, but I could not hear them clearly.”

After several more minutes, certain Director Luo knew nothing else, Chen Ge left the office.

The Third Sick Hall’s door must be more than an ordinary door. Is it like the one in the Haunted House mirror? Does another world lie beyond it?

Unable to understand his parents’ words, he reread the black phone’s mission hint.

It said ‘he’ came from the Third Sick Hall. Does it mean that he came from the bloody world, similar to the mirror monster?

His parents had discussed the Third Sick Hall the day before they vanished. Their disappearance was almost certainly connected to it.

They had disappeared near an abandoned hospital, and police searches of the surrounding buildings found no trace. Perhaps his parents had passed through the door into the other world.

It’s still too soon to confirm the mission venue for the Third Sick Hall is the hospital that my parents disappeared in.Chen Ge patted his face lightly to force himself to calm down. Since it was related to his parents, his emotions were unsettled. The mission has three stars, so it must be dangerous. Even if I accept it now, I might not be able to complete it. I’d better focus on the immediate mission for now.

The Hai Ming Apartments Trial Mission was connected to the Third Sick Hall. Completing it might reveal more, making it the logical place to begin.

At 4:00 p.m., visitor traffic slowed. Chen Ge gave Xu Wan the Haunted House key and went to the Props Room to prepare. His parents’ doll housed the park’s guardian spirit and had no power beyond the grounds, so he left it behind.

After considering his options, he packed a phone charger, lighter, safety rope, and the ever-useful multipurpose mallet.

That should be enough.He thought about it before shoving the reward money that he had left from the Ping An Apartment case into his backpack. It’s early. Perhaps I should go to the mannequin shop first. If the price is right, I can directly give the down payment.

The sooner he completed Mu Yang High School’s Hidden Mission, the sooner he could claim its reward. After tidying up, he passed the dressing room and spotted Xiaoxiao hiding behind the door. Fake blood covered the floor and streaked the doll.

“What have you been doing?” Chen Ge picked up Xiaoxiao, asked Xu Wan to clean the room, and returned to the staff break room. She must think I spilled all that fake blood. Will she decide her boss has lost his mind?

Chen Ge used a towel to wipe the fake blood off Xiaoxiao’s body. He pinched her face, threatening, “If you continue to be naughty, I’ll…”

The threat died because he could not imagine anything that frightened Xiaoxiao. With an exasperated huff, he put her in his backpack. Once everything was ready, he left the Haunted House and the park.

Park attendance had fallen so low that the outdoor parking lot stood empty. Even the bus stop had no queue.

Maintaining the park requires plenty of money; with so few visitors, it mustn’t be easy for Director Luo.

After crossing the road, Chen Ge followed the online directions to the mannequin workshop.

Its sign hung above a stairwell. A nearby vendor confirmed that the workshop was underground.

Graffiti covered the stairwell walls. At the bottom, a glass door bore a sign reading FOR RENT OR SALE.

“Is anyone here?” Through the glass, Chen Ge saw a vast, nearly empty space that resembled a basement warehouse. After a long wait, a slightly overweight man in slippers opened the door.

He appeared close to Chen Ge’s age, dressed casually, with a round, youthful face. When the glass door opened, a blast of cold air struck Chen Ge.

“Are you the owner? I’d like to order some custom mannequins.”

“Okay, come in.” The man invited Chen Ge into the shop. “How big do you want it? If it’s under thirty centimeters, you can get it under three days.”

“That’s too small. I need life-sized figures with articulated joints. Can you make those?” Chen Ge surveyed the equipment. The workshop was far more professional than its entrance suggested.

“Life-sized, with movable parts?” Understanding dawned on the man’s face. “How many?”

“Twenty-four. How quickly can you finish them?”

“Twenty-four?!” the man asked in a raised pitch.

The shout scared Chen Ge. “Why are you screaming so suddenly? Is twenty-four too many for the workshop to produce?”

“All for your personal use?”

“What personal use could I possibly have for twenty-four mannequins?” Realizing the misunderstanding, Chen Ge explained, “I own a Haunted House. They’re for the sets.”

“All right…” The man exhaled. “For a Haunted House, I wouldn’t recommend expensive materials. They’ll suffer too much wear. We make solid and semi-solid models. Prices range from 3,000 to 12,000 RMB each. I should also warn you that every employee has left, so I’m running the place alone. Twenty-four custom figures would take about a month.”
